correctness.rationale: For directed arcs of the fully bidirected Wagner M8 and binary Q3, the face predicate exactly requires distinct incoming/outgoing arcs and no directed cycle, i.e. directed linear forests. An independent source-map enumeration found exactly 6497 faces including empty in each, with common f-vector (24,216,928,2016,2160,1008,144). Independent full unreduced mod2 simplicial boundary reductions have ranks W: (23,193,735,1277,842,134) and cube: (23,193,735,1275,840,132), yielding respective mod2 Betti (4,41,32,10) and (6,45,36,12) in degrees3..6. The actual full verifier and attached complete Morse certificate were inspected: both forward/reverse 24-arc toggle matchings are explicitly checked acyclic on all 6497 augmented faces and 29160 Hasse incidences. Integral gradient-projection Morse matrices have Wagner ∂4 rank11 (unit factors), ∂5=∂6=0, and cube ∂4 rank2, ∂5 rank4, ∂6=0; exact unimodular row/column eliminations leave only unit invariant factors and zero blocks. This establishes free integral homology, not just observed field ranks. No homotopy wedge or all-cubic-family assertion is inferred.

originality.rationale: Complete cube integral multipath homology was already published, as was general multipath topology of directed paths, cycles, polygons and some small grids. The new eight-vertex Wagner bidirected integral homology and exact equality of all face-vector coordinates with Q3, contrasted with different full integral Betti vectors, were not in the identified primary or published records. Same underlying Wagner graph has ordinary matching/Morse or four-cut complexes with different face predicates; they cannot imply directed-arc multipath homology. A new natural cubic-graph pair counterexample therefore survives comparison.

value.rationale: The Wagner Möbius ladder and Q3 are two canonical nonisomorphic eight-vertex 3-regular graphs, making equality of the directed-linear-forest f-vector mathematically natural rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. Their different free integral homology ranks give an explicit counterexample to f-vector determination of multipath topology, in several degrees. The exact Wagner groups and same-f-vector phenomenon are useful finite invariants despite absence of an all-cubic theorem.
